Kavita @ Aasu Vishwakarma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18
August, 2023
 1
 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur

Order Sheet
 Cra No. 808 of 2022
 Kavita @ Aasu Vishwakarma S/o Hasib Agariya, aged about 23 years, R/o village
 Kardauni, Ps Lundra, District Surguja Chhattisgarh

---- Ap
 Versus
 State of Chhattisgarh through Station House Officer, Police 
 Bagicha,District Jashpur, Chhattisgarh
 ---Respo
(Cause Title Taken from Case Information System) 18/08/2023

The appellant has been convicted
by judgment dated 31.03.2022 passed in Special Criminal Case under the Sc St Act No. 6 of 2018 by
the learned Special Judge under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of
Atrocities) Act, 1989, Jashpur, District Jashpur, as under:

Offence Under Section Sentence
 376 of Ipc : Life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 
 341/149 of Ipc : Simple Imprisonment and fine of Rs
 100/-
 148 of Ipc : Rigorous imprisonment for 1 year a
 fine of Rs. 100/-
 365/149 of Ipc : Rigorous imprisonment for 4 years 
 fine of Rs. 100/-
435 of Ipc : Rigorous imprisonment for 3 years and
 fine of Rs. 100/-
3(2)(v) of the Sc & St : Life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 100/-.
(Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989
Kavita @ Aasu Vishwakarma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 August, 2023

1

In default of payment of fine amount, further rigorous imprisonment for 2-2 months in all Sections
and the sentences to run concurrently.
Heard Mr. Nishi Kant Sinha, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Mr. Wasim Miyan, learned

Panel Lawyer appearing for the State/respondent, on Ia No. 01/2022, which is an application for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Learned State counsel submits that notice to the complainant has been served.

However, none
appears on her behalf.

It has been argued by Mr. Sinha, learned counsel for the appellant that the victim girl (Pw-4) is aged
about 28 years of age and she was having friendship with the appellant.

The victim and the appellant
were engaged in sexual relationship outside of marriage for quite long time which is evident from
the deposition of the victim at paragraph 23.

The appellant had also married the victim but the
parents of the victim were against the said relationship as the appellant was a motor-mechanic.

Later, when the marriage of the victim, who is a Nurse in a Government Hospital was fixed with
another person who was also in government service, the victim eloped with the appellant and
thereafter, the Fir was lodged.

Mr. Sinha further submits that the appellant was on bail during the
trial.

The learned trial court has convicted the appellant without there being any reliable material or
evidence on record.

The conclusion of this appeal is likely to take some time, hence, his conviction
and sentence may kindly be suspended and the appellant may be released on bail.

On the other hand, Mr. Wasim Miyan, learned Panel Lawyer for the State/respondent submits that
the learned trial Court, after appreciating the evidence on record and after examining the
cross-examination of the witnesses, has rightly come to the conclusion regarding guilt of the
appellant, which is just and proper.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials available on record.

Considering the fact that even in the deposition made by the victim before the Court, she has
admitted that she was in relationship with the appellant and had established physical relationship
also and further that her parents were against the said relationship, the appellant was on bail during
the trial, and further that since conclusion of this appeal would take some time, and the appellant is
in jail since 04.03.2022, we deem it appropriate to allow the application (Ia No. 1/2022) for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail, moved by the appellant.
Accordingly, the substantive jail sentence awarded to the appellant- Kavita @ Aasu Vishwakarma by
the learned trial Court is hereby suspended.

He shall be released on bail on his executing bail bond
of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand Only) each with one surety in the like amount to the
satisfaction of the concerned trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on
16.10.2023.

He shall thereafter appear before the concerned trial Court on the date to be given by
the Registry of this Court and shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as is given
Kavita @ Aasu Vishwakarma vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 18 August, 2023
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125474136/
2

to him by the said Court, interval being not less than 6 months, till final disposal of this appeal.
Consequently, Ia No. 1/2022, is allowed.
